text:
cory: quick spike question — we're deciding between sharding a control-plane edge per-customer (one CP-edge cluster per tenant / small shard) vs surfacing a tenant-side proxy inside customer VPCs (tenant-proxy). looking for ops/cost/security tradeoffs.

raj: short list of concerns: egress IP preservation, routing complexity, cost of idle capacity, cert + auth propagation, and observable surface.

katy: agree. from product POV tenant-proxy gives customers stronger IP-preservation and local egress control. downside: we surface more infra to the customer (config, lifecycle).

sam: sharded CP-edge (us-hosted per-tenant shards) pros: we control rollout/certs/patches, single TLS termination point, easier tracing. cons: harder to guarantee stable egress IPs per tenant without per-tenant EIPs or SNAT mappings.

alin: two operational notes: 1) many clouds limit number of ENIs/EIPs per account; per-tenant EIP model will be costly. 2) sharding increases deployment count but reduces blast radius if isolating noisy tenants.

cory: example of routing for tenant-proxy (what we'd ask customers to add):
```
Route table: 10.0.0.0/16 -> local
0.0.0.0/0 -> igw (unchanged)
100.64.0.0/10 -> aws-peering-conn (to redwood tenant-proxy svc)
```
customers must accept a peering/privatelink and route specific ALPHA_CIDR to our proxy.

raj: with tenant-proxy we need to push certs + mTLS creds into customer env or use private endpoint with customer-managed endpoint? both increase onboarding friction.

katy: can we combine: surface a lightweight tenant-proxy for egress-preservation-only and still route control/updates through sharded cp-edge? that reduces full lifecycle responsibility for customers.

sam: hybrid makes sense. pattern:
- data path (inference requests) -> tenant-proxy in customer VPC (preserve egress IPs, local network policies)
- control plane (rollouts, metrics) -> sharded cp-edge owned by us (centralized auth/telemetry)
this splits security boundary but doubles integration points.

alin: operational checklist for hybrid: automated cert rotation for proxy, health probes from cp-edge, observable metrics at both hops, and fallback rules (if tenant-proxy down, route to default cp-edge with opt-in).

cory: fallback semantics are key. we need a safe default that keeps customers online but makes it explicit lost IP-preservation. idea: route priority 100 -> tenant-proxy, priority 200 -> cp-edge egress NAT. documented opt-in. thoughts?

raj: yes + add a flag on customer config: "egress_preserve": true|false. If true we allocate egress resources (EIP or NAT gateway) and require peer. If false we fallback to shared NAT and log regression.

katy: perf note: extra hop may add ~10-30ms depending on path. for low-latency customers we should offer dedicated sharded cp-edge in their region.

eng-sre-bot: deploy-bot: FYI: created spike branch cp-edge/egress-hybrid-spike. Link: https://stash/redwood/cp-edge/egress-hybrid-spike :partyparrot:

cory: next steps: (1) write small RFC describing hybrid pattern + fallback semantics, (2) prototype a tenant-proxy container with cert auto-rotation and small CPU footprint, (3) cost projection for per-tenant EIP vs proxy + peering. I'll draft RFC and share. thanks all. :thumbsup:
